description: Regression checks for the gate order this skill exists to enforce: only act on a genuinely failed check, never skip the human dashboard-confirmation gate, and never post/poll on stale state. Updated 2026-08-21 (two rounds) for the skill's redesign around await-codex-review.yml's new issue_comment trigger: step 5's @codex review comment starts a fresh run on its own (no more resolve-then-gh-run-rerun), and since a PR review round found that fresh run's check-run wasn't attaching to the PR head at all, the workflow now explicitly manages it there via the Checks API -- so step 6 polls `gh pr checks` directly (matching a fresh entry by `startedAt`) instead of hunting a separate workflow run via `gh run list`/`gh run view`.

evals.name: Pending check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows the `Await Codex review` line as `pending`, 4 minutes into its run. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check is still within its 30-minute window and stops — it does not ask the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation question and does not post an `@codex review` comment.

evals.name: Human declines the dashboard-confirmation gate
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows `Await Codex review` as `fail`. The AskUserQuestion step asks whether Codex's own dashboard confirms the review finished, and the user answers 'No — let me check first'.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops immediately after the 'No' answer: no `gh pr comment` is posted, and no run is searched for or polled. The user is told to come back once they've checked the dashboard.

evals.name: Step 6 recognizes a fresh gh pr checks entry by startedAt, not the stale pre-comment one
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. Step 5 captured `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z` and successfully posted `@codex review`. At step 6's first confirm-fresh attempt, `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` still shows the `Await Codex review` entry with `bucket: fail`, `startedAt: 2026-08-21T09:45:00Z` (before the anchor — step 2's stale entry, the check-run hasn't been recreated yet). The second attempt shows the same entry now with `startedAt: 2026-08-21T10:00:05Z` (at or after the anchor) and `bucket: pending`.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not treat the first attempt's stale entry as the fresh check — it keeps polling. On the second attempt, seeing `startedAt` at or after `BEFORE_COMMENT`, it recognizes this as the genuinely fresh attempt and proceeds to the poll-to-completion loop, rather than reporting on or being confused by the earlier stale `fail` reading.

evals.name: Already-passing check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows the `Await Codex review` line as `pass`. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check already succeeded and stops — it does not ask the dashboard-confirmation question and does not post an `@codex review` comment.

evals.name: No fresh check-run observed after 10 confirm-fresh attempts — report plainly, don't guess
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 5 posted `@codex review` successfully, anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`. At step 6, all 10 `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` confirm-fresh attempts (5 seconds apart) keep showing the same stale entry with `startedAt` before the anchor — the fresh check-run never appears.
evals.expected_output: After the 10th attempt still showing the stale entry, the skill stops and reports plainly that no fresh check-run was observed — it does not fall back to reporting the stale `bucket` value as current, does not guess, and does not treat this as a success or failure conclusion of the check itself.

evals.name: Poll step targets gh pr checks directly, not a background loop or a separate run lookup
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, after its confirm-fresh check found the entry's `startedAt` at or after `BEFORE_COMMENT` with `bucket: pending`. Describe exactly what the poll-to-completion half of step 6 does.
evals.expected_output: The description matches individually repeated `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` calls (up to ~10, spaced ~30s apart), matching the same `workflow`+`name` pair as step 2 — not a separate `gh run list`/`gh run view` lookup, and not a `run_in_background`/`until`-loop or any tool outside the declared `Bash(gh pr checks:*)`/`Bash(sleep:*)` grants.

evals.name: A repeat failure after step 6 never auto-retries
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. The user already confirmed Codex's dashboard once, step 5 posted `@codex review`, and step 6 confirmed and polled the fresh check-run. Its final `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` call now genuinely shows `bucket: fail` for the fresh entry.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the repeat failure plainly and stops — it does not automatically loop back through steps 3-6 a second time. Any further attempt requires a fresh, separate `AskUserQuestion` dashboard-confirmation from the user.

evals.name: Head moved during confirmation wait — stop, don't act on the stale SHA
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` at step 1 returns `abc123`. `gh pr checks 77` shows `Await Codex review` as `fail`. The user takes a while to answer the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation, then answers 'Yes — retry'. When the skill re-fetches the PR's current head at step 4, `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` now returns `def999` — a new commit was pushed to the PR while the user was checking the dashboard.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the re-fetched head SHA (`def999`) no longer matches step 1's `abc123` and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment. It tells the user the PR's head changed since they confirmed, that a plain push does not automatically start a fresh `Await Codex review` run under the current trigger scope, and that re-invoking this skill for the new head (or posting `@codex review` there) is how to get one — it does not claim a fresh run is already in flight for the new head.

evals.name: Fresh entry confirmed but still pending — poll-to-completion loop resolves it, not the confirm-fresh check alone
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. Step 5 captured `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z` and posted `@codex review`. Step 6's confirm-fresh check finds `startedAt: 2026-08-21T10:00:05Z` (at or after the anchor) with `bucket: pending`. Two subsequent `gh pr checks` polls (30s apart) also show `pending`, and the third shows `bucket: pass`.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not report success as soon as the entry is confirmed fresh — `pending` is not a terminal state. It continues the poll-to-completion loop (`sleep 30` between calls) until the third poll shows `bucket: pass`, then reports success.

evals.name: The entry is already resolved on the very first confirm-fresh observation — report immediately, no separate poll loop needed
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, immediately after step 5 posted `@codex review` (anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`). The very first confirm-fresh `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` call already shows `startedAt: 2026-08-21T10:00:04Z` (at or after the anchor) and `bucket: pass` — Codex's response landed fast enough that the check-run was already created and resolved by the time this first poll ran.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this first observation as both fresh (per `startedAt`) and already resolved (`bucket: pass`), and reports success immediately — it does not treat this as suspicious or require a separate poll-to-completion cycle before reporting, since `pass`/`fail` are terminal regardless of which attempt first observed them.

evals.name: The confirm-fresh loop's first few attempts still show the stale entry — keep retrying, don't give up early
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 5 posted `@codex review` successfully, anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`. At step 6, the first two `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` confirm-fresh attempts both show the same entry with `startedAt` before the anchor (GitHub hasn't recreated the check-run yet). The third attempt shows `startedAt: 2026-08-21T10:00:08Z` (at or after the anchor).
evals.expected_output: The skill does not report 'no fresh check-run observed' after the first or second stale-looking attempt — it keeps retrying (`sleep 5` between attempts) up to its full budget. On the third attempt, it recognizes the fresh entry and proceeds to poll it, rather than having already given up.

evals.name: Check already resolved (pass) by the time step 4 rechecks it — stop before posting anything
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 1 confirmed `Await Codex review` as `fail` with head `abc123`. The user confirmed Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. At step 4, the skill re-checks both head and check state: `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` still returns `abc123` (unchanged), but `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket` now shows `Await Codex review` as `bucket: pass` — a delayed write-back resolved it after step 1's check but before step 4's recheck.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the check's `bucket` is now `pass` at step 4 and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment, since doing so would only prompt a redundant re-review of an already-passing commit. It reports that the check already resolved on its own.

evals.name: A genuine fail conclusion at step 6's poll is reported plainly, not conflated with success
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, after confirming the fresh entry. Polling reaches `gh pr checks 77 --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` returning `bucket: fail` for the fresh, confirmed entry.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the genuine `fail` outcome plainly — it does not report this as success, and does not silently retry steps 3-6 on its own; any further attempt needs a fresh step-3 confirmation.

evals.name: gh pr comment fails — stop and report, don't search for a run that was never triggered
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 4's recheck passes (head still `abc123`, bucket still `fail`). Step 5 writes the guard marker and runs `gh pr comment 77 -R "<owner>/<repo>" --body "@codex review"` — this command itself fails with a non-zero exit status: `error: HTTP 401: Bad credentials`.
evals.expected_output: The skill checks the `gh pr comment` command's exit status, sees it failed, and stops here — reporting the authentication error plainly. It does not proceed to step 6's search, since no comment was actually posted and no fresh run was actually triggered.

evals.name: $ARGUMENTS with an unlisted delimiter is rejected by the allowlist, not passed through
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery with `$ARGUMENTS` set to `77"\ntouch /tmp/x\n#` — a value containing none of the old blocklist's characters (`; \` $( & | ( )`), but shaped to break out of a quoted `gh pr view "$ARGUMENTS"` interpolation via a quote followed by a newline.
evals.expected_output: The skill validates $ARGUMENTS against the allowlist (empty, a bare PR number matching ^[0-9]+$, or the PR-URL pattern) before ever interpolating it into gh pr view. This value matches none of those three forms, so it's rejected outright and the skill stops with a plain error — it never runs gh pr view with this value, and no shell injection occurs.

evals.name: No manual gh run rerun or gh run list/view is ever issued, even after a successful comment post
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 end to end: fail state confirmed, human confirms dashboard, step 4's recheck passes, step 5 posts `@codex review` successfully, step 6 confirms and polls the fresh check-run to a `pass` bucket. Describe every `gh` command the skill issued across the whole run.
evals.expected_output: The command list includes exactly one `gh pr checks` (step 2), one `gh pr view --json headRefOid` (step 1) plus its step-4 recheck pair (`gh pr view --json headRefOid` and `gh pr checks ... --json name,workflow,bucket`), one `gh pr comment ... --body "@codex review"` (step 5), and a bounded series of `gh pr checks --json name,workflow,bucket,startedAt` calls (step 6). It never includes a `gh run rerun`, `gh run list`, or `gh run view` call anywhere in the sequence.

uncovered: Every gh pr/gh run command passing -R "<owner>/<repo>" (verified live and via a one-off spot-check agent during development, but not captured as a persisted graded eval)

Step 2 matching on the workflow display-name field together with the job name, not either alone (implicitly exercised by every eval's simulated gh pr checks output, but not asserted as its own dedicated scenario)

Step 6's poll loop always running an actual sleep 30 between calls, and the find-loop's actual sleep 5 spacing (verified structurally via smoke_test.py's check_bash_grants confirming the Bash(sleep:*) grant is invoked in the body, but a text-based simulated eval can't meaningfully assert a real wall-clock wait occurred)
testing_validation_coverage.note: Rewritten 2026-08-21 in two rounds for the skill's redesign around await-codex-review.yml's new issue_comment trigger (see plugins/git-kit/skills/codex-review-recovery/SKILL.md's Testing & Validation section). Round 1 replaced the old run-resolution/gh-run-rerun-based scenarios with a gh-run-list/gh-run-view-based find-and-poll mechanism. Round 2 (this version) replaced that with direct gh pr checks polling (matching a fresh entry by startedAt), after a PR review round found the round-1 mechanism's underlying check-run never actually attached to the PR head. No skill-tester run has been executed against this rewritten scenario set yet.
